by calling self._auto_save(). This ensures data is persisted on application exit.

Args:
    event (QCloseEvent): The close event object.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    None explicitly raised. Delegates to self._auto_save() if applicable.

jelly_rancher_studio.py.name: default
jelly_rancher_studio.py.description:
Custom JSON serialization handler for PyQt6 objects (JSONEncoder.default override).

This method checks if the object is a PyQt6 instance and, if so, represents it as a string
'<ClassName>' to prevent serialization errors. Otherwise, delegates to the parent class.

Used internally by QtObjectEncoder in _capture_gui_state for dumping widget trees.

Args:
    obj: The object to serialize into JSON.

Returns:
    str: A string representation '<ClassName>' for PyQt6 objects, or the result from
        super().default(obj) otherwise.

Raises:
    None explicitly raised.

launch_gui.py.name: _get_venv_python
launch_gui.py.description:
Locates and returns the path to the Python interpreter executable within the project's
'.venv' virtual environment directory if it exists, otherwise returns None.

The path is platform-specific:
- On Windows (sys.platform.startswith('win')): ``project_root / '.venv' / 'Scripts' / 'python.exe'``
- On other platforms: ``project_root / '.venv' / 'bin' / 'python'``

Args:
    project_root (pathlib.Path): The absolute path to the root directory of the project.

Returns:
    pathlib.Path | None: The path to the '.venv' Python interpreter if the executable exists,
        otherwise None.

Raises:
    None. This function performs a simple existence check and does not raise exceptions.

launch_gui.py.name: main
launch_gui.py.description:
Main entry point for launching the Jelly Rancher Studio GUI application from the
``launch_gui.py`` script.

Determines the project root as the parent directory of this script, ensures it is on
``sys.path``, and attempts to run the GUI using the project's '.venv' Python interpreter
if available:

1. If the current interpreter (``sys.executable``) matches the venv Python, imports
   ``jelly_rancher_studio.main`` and executes it directly.
2. If venv Python exists but is not current, spawns a subprocess to run
   ``jelly_rancher_studio.py`` using the venv interpreter.
3. Otherwise, prints a warning and imports/executes ``jelly_rancher_studio.main``
   using the current interpreter.

Args:
    None

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    ImportError: If ``from jelly_rancher_studio import main`` fails when running directly.
    subprocess.SubprocessError: Potentially if the spawned subprocess encounters issues,
        though ``subprocess.call`` returns the exit code without raising (caller must check
        return value if needed).

scripts\\_common\\media_utils.py.name: clean_episode_title
scripts\\_common\\media_utils.py.description:
Clean episode title by removing technical tags, quality indicators, and normalizing formatting.

Removes common technical tags found in episode titles:
- Quality tags: 2160p, 1080p, 720p, 480p, SD, HD, UHD, 4K
- Release tags: DSNP, Vyndros, WEB-DL, BluRay, HDTV, WEBRip, DVDRip
- File tags: x264, x265, HEVC, AVC, AAC, DTS, AC3
- Scene tags: PROPER, REPACK, INTERNAL, READNFO
- Size/format tags: DD5.1, DTS-HD, TrueHD
- Parenthetical notes: (Part 1), (1), (2), etc.

Also normalizes whitespace and punctuation.

Args:
    title: Raw episode title
    
Returns:
    Cleaned episode title
    
Examples:
    "Heart of Ice (1)" → "Heart of Ice"
    "The Last Laugh 2160p DSNP" → "The Last Laugh"
    "Cat Scratch Fever WEB-DL" → "Cat Scratch Fever"

scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.name: _find_by_provider_ids
scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.description:
Finds a metadata entry in the canonical database using TMDB ID or TVDB ID.

Searches first for the TMDB ID (if provided) in both 'movies' and 'tv_shows' lists.
If no TMDB match is found, searches for the TVDB ID (if provided) in 'tv_shows' only.
String conversion is used for ID comparisons to handle type differences.

Args:
    tmdb_id (Optional[str]): TMDB provider ID to search for. Prioritized in search.
    tvdb_id (Optional[str]): TVDB provider ID to search for (TV shows only).

Returns:
    Optional[Dict[str, Any]]: The first matching metadata dictionary from the canonical
database, or None if no match found.

Raises:
    None.

scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.name: _extract_title_from_filename
scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.description:
Extracts and cleans a media title from the stem of a file path.

Applies regex cleaning to remove:
- Years in parentheses: (?\d{4})?
- Quality/resolution tags: 1080p, 720p, 2160p, 4K, BluRay, etc. (case-insensitive)
- Episode markers: S\d+E\d+ (case-insensitive)
- Bracketed content: [.*?] or (.*?)
Replaces '.', '_' with spaces, normalizes multiple spaces, and strips.

Args:
    path (Path): Pathlib Path object to the media file.

Returns:
    Optional[str]: Cleaned title string, or None if empty after processing.

Raises:
    None.

scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.name: _fuzzy_match_canonical
scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.description:
Performs fuzzy string matching of a title against all canonical database entries.

Combines 'movies' and 'tv_shows' lists. Uses fuzzywuzzy's fuzz.ratio on lowercased
titles, normalized to a 0.0-1.0 score. Returns the highest-scoring match.

Args:
    title (str): Title string to match against canonical metadata titles.

Returns:
    Tuple[Optional[Dict[str, Any]], float]: (best matching metadata dict, match score).
    Score is 0.0 if no items or perfect 1.0 match.

Raises:
    None.

scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.name: _matches_episode
scripts\\core\\action_plan_generator.py.description:
Determines if a proposed operation's destination matches a TV episode.

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Initialize the CanonicalDBDialog.

Sets up the PyQt dialog instance, including logger, key instance attributes for state
management (analysis file, canonical DB, worker thread), and initializes the UI layout.
This dialog provides a GUI for selecting an analysis file and building a canonical database

Returns:

Raises:

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.name: run
scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Execute the canonical database building process.

This method performs the core work of loading the analysis file, processing each detected
media item via metadata lookup (movies via lookup_movie, TV shows via lookup_tv_show),
constructing a structured canonical database, optionally saving it, and emitting progress
updates throughout. Lookup failures are collected separately.

The canonical database is a dict with keys:
- 'timestamp': ISO format datetime string
- 'total_items': int count of processed items
- 'movies': list of metadata dicts with 'original_detection' added
- 'tv_shows': list of metadata dicts with 'original_detection' added
- 'lookup_failures': list of original items that failed lookup

Progress is emitted frequently with percentage (0-100) and status messages. Errors are
handled gracefully and emitted via signal.

Args:
    None

Returns:
    None

Emits:
    progress_update (int, str): Current progress percentage and status message.
    db_complete (Dict[str, Any]): The fully built canonical database.
    db_error (str): Error message string on any failure (file I/O, JSON parse, lookup errors).

Raises:
    None: All exceptions are caught, logged implicitly via emits, and handled via db_error signal.

Prompts the user to select an output JSON file path. If an analysis file is
selected and output path provided, disables input buttons, resets UI progress
and results, creates a `CanonicalDBWorker` instance, connects its progress,

thread.

This slot is connected to the worker's progress_update signal.

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Handles successful completion of the database build.

Stores the canonical database, updates progress to 100%, computes statistics
(movies, TV shows, failures), generates and displays HTML-formatted results
in the results text widget (including top 10 failures if any), shows an
information QMessageBox with summary, logs the results, and accepts/closes
the dialog.

Args:
    canonical_db (Dict[str, Any]): The completed canonical database dictionary
        containing 'movies', 'tv_shows', 'lookup_failures', etc.

This slot is connected to the worker's db_complete signal.

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Handle build errors during canonical database construction.

Updates the UI elements to reflect the failure state: sets the progress label to indicate
failure, re-enables the file selection and build buttons, displays an HTML-formatted error
message in the results text area, shows a critical QMessageBox dialog with the error details,
and logs the error using the dialog's logger.

Args:

    error (str): The error message describing what went wrong during the database build.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    None

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.name: closeEvent
scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Override of QWidget.closeEvent to handle dialog closure gracefully.

If a background worker thread is running, it terminates the worker and waits for it to finish
before accepting the close event. This ensures clean shutdown and prevents resource leaks.

Args:
    self: The CanonicalDbDialog instance.
    event (QCloseEvent): The close event triggered by the user or system.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    None

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.name: progress_callback
scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Callback invoked during database build to report and emit progress updates.

Calculates the progress percentage based on current and total items, constructs a status
message, and emits the progress_update signal with the percentage and status for UI updates.

Args:
    current (int): The current number of items processed (1-based in status).
    total (int): The total number of items to process.
    item_name (str): The name or title of the item currently being processed.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    ZeroDivisionError: If total is zero (handled by defaulting progress to 0).

scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.name: build_with_progress
scripts\\core\\dialogs\\canonical_db_dia.description:
Builds a canonical database from a list of detected media items with progress reporting.

Initializes a database dictionary with timestamp and total items count. Iterates over each
media item, emits progress updates starting from 15%, performs metadata lookup based on
media type ('movie' or 'tv_show') using approximate year, stores successful lookups with
original detection data or adds failures to a dedicated list. At 90% progress, optionally
saves the database to the specified path. Emits final 100% completion signal.

Args:
    detected_media (list[dict]): List of detected media dictionaries, each containing
        at least 'title' (str), 'type' ('movie' or 'tv_show'), and optionally 'year_estimate' (int).
    output_path (Optional[pathlib.Path], optional): File path to save the JSON database.
        Defaults to None (no save).

Returns:
    dict: Canonical database structure with keys:
        - 'timestamp' (str): ISO format build time.
        - 'total_items' (int): Number of input items.
        - 'movies' (list[dict]): Successfully looked-up movie metadata.
        - 'tv_shows' (list[dict]): Successfully looked-up TV show metadata.
        - 'lookup_failures' (list[dict]): Items with failed lookups.

Raises:
    Exception: From lookup.lookup_movie(), lookup.lookup_tv_show(), or lookup.save_database()

class.

If the test was successful (`success=True`), displays an information message box

message.

This is a private slot method connected to the `test_complete` signal of
`JellyfinTestWorker`.

    message (str): A descriptive message about the test result.

If integration is enabled:

  - If valid, saves the server URL and API key to the config manager.

scripts\\core\\file_scanner.py.name: _scan_recursive

Recursively scan a folder and all subdirectories for files matching configured extensions.

Optimized single-pass traversal using `pathlib.Path.rglob('*')` with immediate filtering
by extension, exclusion checks, and processing. Provides progress feedback every 10 files
via `self.progress_callback`. Skips inaccessible files and logs errors without stopping.

Args:

Returns:
  List[FileRecord]: List of processed `FileRecord` objects for matching files.

Raises:
  None: PermissionError and OSError are caught and skipped per-file; other Exceptions
  are caught at the traversal level, logged, and added to `self.statistics.errors`.

Scan only the top-level contents of a single folder (non-recursive).

exclusion checks, and processing. Provides progress feedback every 10 files via
`self.progress_callback`. Skips inaccessible files and logs errors.

Args:
  folder_path (pathlib.Path): Directory to scan at top level only.

Returns:
  List[FileRecord]: List of processed `FileRecord` objects for matching files.

Raises:
  None: PermissionError and OSError are caught and skipped per-file; other Exceptions
  are caught at the iteration level, logged as warnings, and added to `self.statistics.errors`.

scripts\\core\\file_scanner.py.name: _format_size
scripts\\core\\file_scanner.py.description:
Formats a size in bytes into a human-readable string representation using
IEC binary prefixes (e.g., KiB, MiB are approximated as KB, MB).

This static method converts integer byte sizes into strings like '1.2 MB' or '3.4 GB',
rounding to one decimal place. It supports sizes up to petabytes (PB).

Args:
    size_bytes (int): The size in bytes to format. Assumes a non-negative integer;
        negative values will produce negative formatted strings (e.g., '-1.0 B').

Returns:
    str: A human-readable string representation of the size (e.g., '512.0 B', '1.0 KB',
        '1.5 MB', '2.3 GB', '4.5 TB', '1.0 PB').

Raises:
    None.

Examples:
    >>> _format_size(0)
    '0.0 B'
    >>> _format_size(512)
    '512.0 B'
    >>> _format_size(1024)
    '1.0 KB'
    >>> _format_size(1500)
    '1.5 KB'
    >>> _format_size(1024**3)
    '1.0 GB'
    >>> _format_size(1024**5 * 2)
    '2.0 PB'

Note:
    Uses base-1024 divisions with one decimal place precision. For very large sizes
    beyond 1024 TB, falls back to PB.

scripts\\core\\inventory_repository.py.description:
CLI entry point for testing the InventoryRepository.

This function serves as a command-line interface (CLI) to interact with the
inventory database. It supports displaying database statistics, recent scan
history, clearing all data (with confirmation), or printing help if no options
are provided. Logging is configured to INFO level.

Command-line arguments:
  --db (str, default='data/inventory.db'): Path to the SQLite database file.
  --stats (flag): Display comprehensive database statistics as JSON.
  --history (flag): Show the last 20 scan sessions as JSON.
  --clear (flag): WARNING - Clears all data from the database after user
      confirmation (type 'yes').

Returns:
  int: Always 0, indicating successful execution.

Raises:
  SystemExit: Implicitly via argparse if invalid arguments are provided.
  sqlite3.Error: If database operations (stats, history, clear) fail due to
      connection or query issues.
  ValueError: Potentially from repository methods during data retrieval.

_initialize_database(self)

Private method to create the database schema if tables do not exist.

Initializes two core tables:
- `files`: Stores file inventory details including id (PK), scan_session_id (FK),
  absolute_path (unique), size_bytes, extension, parent_folder, scan_timestamp,
  md5_hash, created_at.
- `scan_sessions`: Stores scan metadata including id (PK), root_folder,
  scan_start, scan_end, total_files, total_size_bytes, recursive, error_count,
  notes.

Creates indexes on files(parent_folder), files(extension), files(scan_session_id)
for query performance.

Args:
  self: InventoryRepository instance.

Returns:
  None

Raises:
  sqlite3.Error: If connection fails or schema creation/execution encounters an
      error (e.g., invalid SQL, permissions, disk space).

corresponding 'docstring'. If not found, falls back to any matching 'docstring'.
Returns appropriate error messages if no index or no match.

Args:

    function_name (str): The name of the function to look up.

scripts\\core\\jelly_rancher_main.py.name: scan_organization_folder

Validates that a folder path is provided in `org_folder_input`. Clears the
organization log, summary, and resets progress bar. Dynamically adds the 'media'
subdirectory to sys.path to import `MediaFileScanner`. Performs the following:

1. Scans the folder for media files using `MediaFileScanner.scan_files()`.
2. Analyzes the folder structure with `analyze_folder_structure()`.
3. Formats and displays a summary in `org_summary`.
4. Updates progress bar and log with emojis and timestamps throughout.
5. Stores results in `self.current_scan_files` and `self.current_scan_structure`.

Returns:

Raises:

        displayed in a critical QMessageBox, and progress is not fully updated.

- org_type from `media_type_combo`
- dry_run from `org_dry_run` checkbox
- create_snapshot=True
- verify_integrity from `org_verify` checkbox

scripts\\core\\jelly_rancher_main.py.name: execute_batch
scripts\\core\\jelly_rancher_main.py.description:
Execute selected batch file operations with safety checks, dry-run option,
and pre-execution snapshot.

Collects enabled operations from self.batch_action_table excluding 'Skip' and
'Review' actions. Supports dry-run mode (logs planned actions without executing).
For live execution:
- Confirms with user via message box showing operation counts (move/copy/delete).
- Creates a snapshot of the source directory using SnapshotManager.
- Executes operations using shutil.move/copy2 or Path.unlink.
- Updates table status, progress bar, and log in real-time.
- Journals the result.

Ensures destination parent directories exist.

Side effects:
- Modifies filesystems (move/copy/delete).
- Updates self.batch_action_table statuses, self.batch_log, self.batch_progress.
- Creates snapshot and shows confirmation/success/error messages.
- Calls self.journal_action.

Args:
    None

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Snapshot creation or execution errors are caught, logged, and shown
        in message boxes; aborts execution without reraise.

scripts\\core\\jelly_rancher_main.py.name: manage_credentials
scripts\\core\\jelly_rancher_main.py.description:
Opens a modal QDialog for managing stored credentials with full add, update, and delete
functionality using CredentialManager.

The dialog features:
- A QListWidget displaying stored credentials (TMDB API Key noted as managed in Settings)
  and credentials from CredentialManager.list_credentials().
- Delete button: Confirms and deletes selected credential (TMDB protected), refreshes list.
- Add/Update form: Credential key input, password-masked value input with toggle visibility
  button, and Save button to store via CredentialManager.set_credential().
- Help text explaining secure storage and examples (e.g., opensubtitles_username,

This private method provides a connection to the database file at `self.db_path`
with row_factory set to `sqlite3.Row` for dictionary-like row access. It ensures
proper transaction handling:

* Commits changes on successful context exit.
* Rolls back on any exception.

Intended for use in `with` statements within other methods of the class.

scripts\\core\\regex_analysis_worker.py.name: run
scripts\\core\\regex_analysis_worker.py.description:
Execute hybrid (regex + LLM) media structure analysis in a background thread.

This two-phase method first runs regex analysis on `self.scanned_files` to detect
media items. Low/medium confidence items trigger Phase 2, sending ambiguous cases to
an LLM-based analyzer using `self.model`. Results are merged: high-confidence from
regex plus LLM detections. Combined reorganization plan, multi-part episodes, and
metadata (including cost savings from skipping LLM on high-confidence items) are
produced. Progress, results, and errors are emitted via signals.

Requires `self.folder_structure` (for project_name) and `self.model` (for LLM).

Args:
    None

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    None. All exceptions are caught, logged with traceback, and emitted via the `error`
    signal.

Emits:
    progress (str): Detailed phase updates, e.g., regex detection counts, ambiguous
        count, LLM phase start, merging, and completion.
    finished (dict): Combined result with:
        - 'detected_media' (list): Final media list (regex high-conf + LLM).
        - 'reorganization_plan' (dict): Merged summary, folder_changes, jellyfin_compliance_issues.
        - 'multi_part_episodes' (list): Merged from both analyzers.
        - 'reasoning' (str): Concatenated regex and LLM reasoning.
        - 'metadata' (dict): 'analyzer': 'hybrid', item counts, cost_savings percentage.
    error (str): Error message, e.g., 'Hybrid analysis failed: <exception>'.

scripts\\core\\tmdb_backend.py.name: _rate_limit
scripts\\core\\tmdb_backend.py.description:
Enforces courteous rate limiting between consecutive TMDB API requests.

This private method ensures that API calls respect TMDB's rate limits by checking
the elapsed time since the last request (stored in ``self.last_request_time``).
If the elapsed time is less than ``self.min_request_interval`` (typically 1 second),
it sleeps for the difference, logs a debug message, and updates the timestamp.

TMDB guidelines recommend an upper limit of ~40 requests per second and strict
respect for 429 (Too Many Requests) responses. This implementation adopts a
conservative approach of 1 request per second to prioritize reliability and
courtesy.

Args:
    None

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    None

Checks if the 'scanned_files' table exists in the database:
- If exists, logs detection and records migration as 'Base schema with scanned_files table'.
- If not, logs fresh install and records as 'Fresh installation - base schema'.

This migration does NOT create or alter tables; it only initializes tracking
at v1 to accommodate pre-existing schemas without data loss.

Args:
    self: The DatabaseMigrator instance.
    conn (sqlite3.Connection): Open database connection.

scripts\\database\\migrations.py.name: _migration_v2_project_management
scripts\\database\\migrations.py.description:
Migration v2: Adds project management tables and links existing scanned_files to a default project.

This private migration method applies database schema changes for project management functionality.
It executes SQL schema definitions from 'schema.sql' to create new tables, conditionally modifies
the 'scanned_files' table to support project associations, creates a default 'Legacy Scans' project
for backward compatibility, and records the migration completion.

New tables created:
- projects: Stores project information.
- project_scan_sessions: Tracks scan sessions within projects.
- project_analyses: Holds analysis results for projects.
- project_action_plans: Manages action plans derived from analyses.
- project_operations: Records operations performed on projects.
- project_state: Manages project states.

If 'scanned_files' exists without 'project_id':
- Adds 'project_id INTEGER REFERENCES projects(id)' column.
- Creates index 'idx_scanned_files_project' on project_id.
- Inserts default project ('Legacy Scans').
- Updates existing rows in 'scanned_files' to use the default project_id.

Logs progress and updated row counts via logger.

Args:
    conn (sqlite3.Connection): Active SQLite database connection used for executing migrations.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: Raised if any SQL execution fails (e.g., schema application, ALTER TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE).
    FileNotFoundError: If the 'schema.sql' file is missing from the migrations directory.
    IOError: If 'schema.sql' cannot be read (e.g., permission issues).
    ValueError: Potentially from datetime.isoformat() or cursor operations if data is invalid.

Note:
    Assumes 'self._record_migration' method exists to log migration completion.
    Path to schema.sql is relative to migrations.py using pathlib.Path.

scripts\\media\\nfo_generator.py.description:
Pretty-formats the given XML string by parsing it with ElementTree and re-serializing it.

This process normalizes the XML representation, ensuring a consistent string output.
If the input is empty or contains only whitespace, it is returned unchanged.

In case of parsing errors (e.g., invalid XML) or other exceptions during formatting,
a warning is logged using the module's logger, and the original string is returned
without raising an exception.

This is a private static method used internally in the NFO generator for handling
XML data in media metadata files.

Args:
    xml_str (str): The input XML string to format.

Returns:
    str: The formatted XML string if parsing succeeds, or the original input
        string if the input is empty/whitespace or if formatting fails.

Raises:
    None: All exceptions (ET.ParseError and general Exception) are caught,
         logged as warnings, and handled gracefully by returning the original string.

Example:
    >>> _format_xml('<root><child>text</child></root>')
    '<root><child>text</child></root>'
    >>> _format_xml('invalid xml')
    'invalid xml'  # Original returned, warning logged

scripts\\media\\regex_structure_analyzer.description:
'''CLI entry point for testing the RegexStructureAnalyzer.

This standalone function provides a command-line interface to scan a specified folder for
media files, analyze their naming structure using regex patterns, and print a comprehensive
summary including detected TV shows and movies, multi-part episodes, and detailed reasoning
about the analysis process.

Usage:
    python regex_structure_analyzer.py <folder_path>

If no folder_path is provided via sys.argv[1], prints usage instructions and exits.

The process involves:
1. Scanning the folder using FileScanner to collect file records.
2. Analyzing the files with RegexStructureAnalyzer to detect media types, titles,
   years, seasons, confidence scores, multi-part episodes, etc.
3. Pretty-printing the results with sections for detected media, multi-part episodes,
   and reasoning.

Args:
    None (relies on sys.argv for input).

Returns:
    None.

Raises:
    ValueError: If folder path is invalid (via Path(sys.argv[1])).
    Any exceptions from FileScanner.scan_folder() or RegexStructureAnalyzer.analyze_structure()
    are not explicitly raised but may cause the script to fail during execution.
'''

scripts\\media\\reorganization_executor..name: generate_report
scripts\\media\\reorganization_executor..description:
Generates a comprehensive human-readable report summarizing the execution of media reorganization operations.

The report includes:

* A formatted header with the report title and current timestamp.
* High-level statistics: total operations, successful operations, failed operations,
  and skipped operations.
* Detailed listing of all failed operations, showing source path, target path,
  and the associated error message for each.
* A breakdown of successful operations by action type (e.g., 'move', 'copy', 'delete'),
  with counts for each type.

This method aggregates data from ``self.results`` (a list of operation result objects),
``self.total_operations``, ``self.successful_operations``, ``self.failed_operations``,
``self.skipped_operations``, and ``self.get_failed_operations()``. It should be called
after operations have been executed to produce a post-execution summary.

Returns:
    str: A multi-line string containing the formatted report, suitable for printing
    or logging.

Raises:
    None. This method performs only string formatting and data aggregation,
    with no external I/O or operations that could raise exceptions.

scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.name: main
scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.description:
Main CLI entry point for generating a media reorganization plan.

Parses command-line arguments, loads LLM analysis results, canonical metadata database,
and optional scan results. Instantiates a `ReorganizationPlanner`, creates the reorganization
plan, prints comprehensive statistics (total actions, by action type, by media type,
subtitles, and path conflicts), and saves the plan as JSON, CSV, or both depending on the
specified format.

Command-line arguments:
    --llm-analysis (str, required): Path to the LLM analysis JSON file.
    --canonical-db (str, required): Path to the canonical metadata database JSON file.
    --scan-results (str, optional): Path to the scan results JSON file.
    --output (str, default='data/reorganization_plans'): Output directory for the plan files.
    --format (str, choices=['json', 'csv', 'both'], default='both'): Output format.

Examples:
    python reorganization_planner.py --llm-analysis analysis.json --canonical-db db.json

Args:
    None

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    FileNotFoundError: If any required input file paths do not exist.
    json.JSONDecodeError: If any JSON file contains invalid JSON.
    argparse.ArgumentError: If command-line arguments are invalid.
    Exception: If `ReorganizationPlanner.create_plan` or save methods fail.

scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.name: _build_subtitle_map
scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.description:
Build a mapping of video files to their associated subtitle files.

Scans all files from scan results, identifies subtitle files based on `SUBTITLE_EXTENSIONS`,
and matches them to corresponding video files (using `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS`) by trying stem
matches in the same directory. Supports Jellyfin naming conventions such as:

- Movie.srt (default subtitle)
- Movie.en.srt (English subtitle)
- Movie.en.forced.srt (forced English subtitle)
- Movie.en.sdh.srt (SDH subtitle)

Populates `self.subtitle_map` as a dict mapping video file paths (str) to lists of subtitle
file paths (str). Logs progress and mapping details.

Args:
    scan_results (Dict[str, Any]): Scan results dictionary with 'all_files' (list of str paths)
        and 'video_files' (list of str paths).

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    KeyError: If 'all_files' or 'video_files' keys are missing from scan_results (though
        mitigated by .get()).
    None: Generally no exceptions raised.

scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.name: _process_media_item
scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.description:
Process a single media item from LLM analysis and generate reorganization actions.

Dispatches to specialized handlers based on media type ('movie' or 'tv_show'). For unknown
types, creates 'REVIEW' actions for each file with associated subtitles from the subtitle map.

Args:
    media_item (Dict[str, Any]): Dictionary representing a detected media item, with keys
        'type' (str), 'files' (list of str), and type-specific fields like 'title', 'episodes'.
    canonical_db (Dict[str, Any]): Canonical metadata database with 'movies' and 'tv_shows' keys.

Returns:
    None

Side Effects:
    Appends `ReorganizationAction` objects to `self.actions`.

Raises:
    None

scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.name: _process_movie
scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.description:
Process movie media item and generate MOVE or REVIEW actions.

Looks up movie metadata in canonical_db['movies'][title]. If metadata exists, creates
'MOVE' actions for each video file to 'Movies/{title (year)}/{title (year).ext}', includes
subtitles via `_create_subtitle_action`, and tracks path conflicts. If no metadata, queues
'REVIEW' actions.

Args:
    media_item (Dict[str, Any]): Movie item with 'title' (str) and 'files' (list of str paths).
    canonical_db (Dict[str, Any]): Database with 'movies' dict mapping titles to metadata
        (including 'year', 'title', 'tmdb_id', 'imdb_id').

Returns:
    None

Side Effects:
    Appends `ReorganizationAction` instances to `self.actions`.
    Updates `self.path_conflicts` with potential target path overlaps.

Raises:
    None

scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.name: _process_tv_show
scripts\\media\\reorganization_planner.p.description:
Process TV show media item and generate MOVE or REVIEW actions.

Looks up show metadata in canonical_db['tv_shows'][title]. For each episode, if metadata
and episode numbers available, creates 'MOVE' action to
'TV Shows/{title}/Season {SS}/{title} S{SS}E{EE}[-E{EE}] [- Episode Title].ext', with subtitles.
Derives episode title from seasons metadata if available. Handles multi-episode files.
Queues 'REVIEW' if missing metadata or episode numbers. Tracks path conflicts.

Args:
    media_item (Dict[str, Any]): TV show item with 'title' (str), 'episodes' (list of dicts
        each with 'file_path', 'season' (int), 'episodes' (list of int)).
    canonical_db (Dict[str, Any]): Database with 'tv_shows' dict mapping titles to metadata
        including 'title', 'tmdb_id', 'imdb_id', 'seasons' (dict of season dicts with episodes).

Returns:
    None

Side Effects:
    Appends `ReorganizationAction` instances to `self.actions`.
    Updates `self.path_conflicts` with potential target path overlaps.

Raises:
    None

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: __init__
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Initialize the Analysis View widget.

Sets up the UI for LLM-powered folder structure analysis and metadata lookup.
This view implements Points 2-3 of the JellyRancher workflow, allowing users to
analyze folder structures and get reorganization recommendations.

Args:
    project: The current Project instance containing scan data and settings
    project_manager: ProjectManager instance for database operations
    parent: Parent QWidget (typically the main application window)
    
Raises:
    Exception: If initialization fails, shows critical error dialog to user
    
Signals:
    analysis_saved(int): Emitted when analysis results are saved to database
    metadata_built(int): Emitted when metadata enrichment is completed

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _init_ui
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Initializes the user interface for the Structure Analysis view in the AnalysisView class.

Creates a comprehensive Qt-based UI layout using QVBoxLayout as the main container.
Configures margins, spacing, and adds the following key components:

- Title QLabel with styled font and color ('Structure Analysis').
- 'Analysis Mode' QGroupBox containing a QComboBox for selecting analysis modes:
  - 🧖 LLM Analysis (Deep, Canonical, API Cost)
  - ⚡ Regex Analysis (Instant, Free, Offline)
  - 🔐 Hybrid (Regex + LLM for Ambiguous)
  Includes tooltips explaining mode differences and cost savings.
- 'LLM Model Selection' QGroupBox with QComboBox for models (Claude-3.7-Sonnet,
  GPT-4, Gemini-2.5-Pro) and a 'Refresh Models' QPushButton connected to
  self._refresh_models.
- Horizontal button layout with:
  - 'Preview Prompt' QPushButton connected to self._preview_prompt.
  - '▶ Run Analysis' QPushButton (styled purple, minimum height 40px) connected
    to self._run_analysis.
  - '✨ Enrich Metadata' QPushButton (styled teal, initially disabled) connected
    to self._enrich_metadata.
- QProgressBar (initially invisible, maximum 0).
- Status QLabel (italic, gray).
- 'Analysis Results' QGroupBox with readonly QTextEdit (placeholder text).
- 'Canonical Metadata Database' QGroupBox with readonly QTextEdit for TMDB/OMDb
  lookup results (placeholder text).

Sets the layout on self, then calls self._load_scan_data() to populate initial data.

Args:
    self: Instance of AnalysisView class.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: If any UI initialization step fails (e.g., Qt widget creation,
        stylesheet parsing, or _load_scan_data()), logs the full traceback,
        displays a critical QMessageBox with error details, and re-raises the
        exception to propagate the failure.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _load_scan_data
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Load scan data from the most recent scan session for the current project.

Retrieves the latest scan session from the database and loads associated file records.
This data is used as input for LLM analysis and metadata enrichment operations.

The method:
1. Connects to the media library database
2. Finds the most recent scan session for the current project
3. Parses scan options to extract folder paths and inventory session IDs
4. Loads all file records from associated inventory sessions
5. Updates UI status to reflect loaded data

If no scan data is found, the UI will show appropriate messaging to the user.

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: If database operations fail
    json.JSONDecodeError: If scan options JSON is malformed

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _use_filtered_data
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Uses pre-filtered data from ScanResultsView, bypassing the normal full database load.

This private method is invoked during AnalysisView initialization when self.filtered_files
is provided (typically passed from a parent ScanResultsView). It optimizes analysis by
using a subset of files, reducing LLM token costs and focusing on relevant content.

Performs the following steps:
1. Assigns self.filtered_files to self.scanned_files.
2. Instantiates FileScanner and builds self.folder_structure from the filtered files,
   updating 'project_name' and 'total_files' fields.
3. Generates a human-readable filter description from self.filter_config (file types,
   size range, duplicates exclusion) if available.
4. Updates self.lbl_status with ready message including file count and filter details
   (green, bold, italic style).
5. Enables self.btn_run and self.btn_preview buttons.
6. Logs the operation details.

If no filtered_files are available, logs a warning and exits early.

Args:
    self: Instance of AnalysisView class.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    None. Exceptions are caught, logged with traceback, status label is updated
        with error message (red implied), and analysis buttons are disabled.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _refresh_models
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Refresh the list of available LLM models from the Poe API.

Queries the Poe API service to get the current list of available models
for analysis. This ensures users can select from the latest available
models and their capabilities.

The method:
1. Updates status label to indicate model fetching
2. Creates a PoeClient instance to query available models
3. Clears and repopulates the model selection dropdown
4. Updates status with success/failure information
5. Shows warning dialog if API query fails

If the API query fails, the UI gracefully degrades by showing
a warning but continuing to function with default model options.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warning if model refresh fails, but doesn't prevent continued use

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _preview_prompt
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Preview the analysis prompt that will be sent to the LLM.

Generates and displays the exact prompt that would be sent to the selected
LLM model for analysis. This allows users to review the context and
instructions before committing to the analysis operation.

The method:
1. Validates that scan data is available for prompt generation
2. Creates an LLMStructureAnalyzer to build the analysis prompt
3. Constructs a preview dialog with the formatted prompt
4. Shows the prompt in a scrollable text area
5. Provides OK/Cancel buttons for user interaction

The preview helps users understand what information the LLM will
receive and ensures the analysis context is appropriate for their needs.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warning if no scan data is available

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _copy_to_clipboard
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Copy the provided text to the system clipboard.

Utility method for copying text content (typically prompts or results)
to the clipboard for external use or sharing.

Args:
    text: The text content to copy to clipboard
    
The method:
1. Accesses the QApplication clipboard instance
2. Sets the provided text as clipboard content
3. Updates status label to confirm successful copy
4. Shows error dialog if clipboard access fails

This is commonly used after prompt preview to allow users to
copy the analysis prompt for external review or manual execution.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warning if clipboard operations fail

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _run_analysis
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Execute analysis on the loaded scan data using the selected mode.

Supports three analysis modes:
- LLM: Deep AI analysis with context understanding (API cost)
- Regex: Fast pattern matching (instant, free, offline)
- Hybrid: Regex first, LLM only for ambiguous (80-90% cost savings)

Initiates the analysis workflow by:
1. Validating that scan data is available
2. Determining selected analysis mode
3. Getting LLM model (if needed for mode)
4. Confirming execution with the user
5. Creating and starting appropriate worker thread
6. Disabling UI controls during processing
7. Showing progress indication

The worker runs in a separate thread to prevent UI blocking.
Progress and completion are handled by connected signal handlers.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows user warnings if no scan data is available

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _on_analysis_progress
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Handle progress updates during LLM analysis.

Updates the UI status label with current analysis progress information.
This method is called periodically by the LLMAnalysisWorker to provide
user feedback during long-running analysis operations.

Args:
    status: Progress status message from the analysis worker
           (e.g., "Analyzing folder structure...", "Querying LLM...")
           
The method simply updates the status label text. If the update fails
(rare), it logs the error but doesn't interrupt the analysis process.

This provides real-time feedback to users during analysis operations
that may take several seconds to minutes depending on content complexity.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _on_analysis_finished
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Handle completion of LLM analysis.

Processes the analysis results and updates the UI to display findings.
This method is called when the LLMAnalysisWorker completes successfully.

Args:
    analysis_result: Dictionary containing analysis results with keys:
        - detected_media: List of detected media items with metadata
        - recommendations: Suggested reorganization actions
        - confidence_scores: Analysis confidence metrics
        - Other analysis-specific data
        
The method:
1. Re-enables UI controls that were disabled during analysis
2. Stores results in instance variables for later use
3. Formats and displays a structured summary of findings
4. Shows detected media items with confidence scores
5. Enables metadata enrichment functionality

The results are formatted for human readability and LLM consumption.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _on_analysis_error
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Handle errors that occur during LLM analysis.

This method is called when the LLMAnalysisWorker encounters an error.
It provides user feedback and restores the UI to a usable state.

Args:
    error_msg: Descriptive error message from the analysis worker
    
The method:
1. Re-enables UI controls that were disabled during analysis
2. Hides the progress bar
3. Updates status label with error information
4. Shows a critical error dialog to inform the user
5. Logs the error for debugging purposes

The UI is restored to allow retry attempts or other operations.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _save_analysis_to_database
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Save analysis results to the project database.

Persists the LLM analysis results for future reference and audit trails.
This allows users to review historical analyses and track changes over time.

Args:
    display_content: Formatted text content for display/storage
    parsed_json: Structured analysis results as dictionary containing:
        - recommendations: List of suggested actions
        - detected_media: Media detection results
        - reorganization_plan: Structural recommendations
        - Other analysis metadata
        
The method:
1. Connects to the media library database
2. Extracts analysis metadata (model, scan ID, confidence)
3. Determines confidence level based on results quality
4. Inserts analysis record into project_analyses table
5. Emits analysis_saved signal to notify other components
6. Updates UI status to reflect successful save

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: If database operations fail
    json.JSONEncodeError: If parsed_json cannot be serialized

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _enrich_metadata
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Start the metadata enrichment process for detected media.

Initiates background metadata lookup using TMDB and OMDb APIs to gather
canonical information for all detected media items. This process resolves
official titles, release years, episode structures, and identifies content
that requires NFO metadata files.

The enrichment process:
1. Validates that detected media data is available from prior analysis
2. Prompts user for confirmation due to API usage
3. Checks for required API keys (TMDB_API_KEY, OMDB_API_KEY)
4. Creates and starts a MetadataLookupWorker thread
5. Disables UI controls during processing
6. Shows progress indication

The worker runs asynchronously to prevent UI blocking. Results are
processed by connected signal handlers when complete.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warnings if no media data or missing API keys

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _on_metadata_progress
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Handle progress updates during metadata enrichment.

Updates the UI with current progress information during metadata lookup
operations. This method is called periodically by the MetadataLookupWorker
to provide detailed progress feedback for long-running API queries.

Args:
    status: Current status message from the metadata worker
           (e.g., "Querying TMDB for 'Movie Title'...")
    current: Number of items processed so far
    total: Total number of items to process
    
The method:
1. Updates the status label with the current status message
2. Sets progress bar maximum and current values for visual progress
3. Logs errors if UI updates fail (rare case)

Progress tracking is important for metadata enrichment as it involves
multiple API calls that can take significant time depending on the
number of media items and API response times.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _on_metadata_finished
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Handle completion of metadata enrichment lookup.

Processes the canonical metadata database and updates the UI to display
the enriched information. This method is called when the MetadataLookupWorker
completes successfully.

Args:
    canonical_db: Dictionary containing canonical metadata with structure:
        - movies: List of movie metadata dictionaries
        - tv_shows: List of TV show metadata dictionaries
        - episodes: Episode metadata for TV shows
        Each item contains TMDb/OMDb canonical information
        
The method:
1. Re-enables UI controls that were disabled during lookup
2. Stores canonical database for later use
3. Formats and displays summary of enriched metadata
4. Shows movies and TV shows with key information
5. Emits metadata_built signal to notify other components
6. Updates status to indicate successful enrichment

The canonical database provides authoritative metadata for content
identification and NFO file generation.

scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.name: _on_metadata_error
scripts\\ui\\analysis_view.py.description:
Handle errors that occur during metadata enrichment.

This method is called when the MetadataLookupWorker encounters an error
during API queries or data processing. It provides user feedback and
restores the UI to a usable state.

Args:
    error_msg: Descriptive error message from the metadata worker
              (may include API errors, network issues, or parsing failures)
    
The method:
1. Re-enables UI controls that were disabled during lookup
2. Hides the progress bar
3. Updates status label with error information
4. Shows a critical error dialog to inform the user
5. Logs the error for debugging purposes

Error handling is robust - if the error handler itself fails,
it includes fallback UI restoration to prevent the interface
from becoming unusable.

Common error causes:
- Missing or invalid API keys
- Network connectivity issues
- API rate limiting or service unavailability
- Malformed response data from external services

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: __init__
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Initialize the ExecutionWorker thread.

Sets up the background worker for executing file operations with
full transaction management, rollback capability, and optional
Jellyfin library refresh.

Args:
    action_plan_id: Database ID of the action plan to execute
    dry_run: If True, simulate operations without actual file changes
    jellyfin_refresh: If True, refresh Jellyfin library after execution
    
The worker provides real-time progress updates and maintains
transaction integrity for all file operations.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: run
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Execute operations with full transaction management.

This is the main execution method that runs in a background thread.
It processes all approved operations from the action plan with proper
transaction handling, progress reporting, and optional Jellyfin integration.

The execution process:
1. Loads approved operations from the database (`project_operations` table
   where `action_plan_id` matches and `user_approved = 1`).
2. Initializes `TransactionManager` for rollback capability.
3. Sets up Jellyfin client if `self.jellyfin_refresh` is enabled and config is valid.
4. Executes each operation (hardcoded as MOVE) with progress updates via
   `self.progress.emit(i, total, message)`.
5. Performs Jellyfin library refresh on modified paths if client is available.
6. Reports final success/failure counts via `self.finished.emit(success_count, fail_count, batch_id)`.

All operations are wrapped in transactions for atomicity using `TransactionManager`.
Progress and logs are reported in real-time via `self.log_message.emit(text)` signals.
Failed operations are logged but do not stop the batch execution.

The method handles dry-run mode (`self.dry_run`) for testing without actual file changes.
In production mode, files are moved using `shutil.move`, MD5 hashes are verified,
and database is updated with execution timestamps and hashes.

Side effects:
- Modifies `data/media_library.db` (updates `project_operations` and `project_action_plans`).
- Moves files from `current_path` to `proposed_path`.
- Creates batch in TransactionManager (`self.batch_id` set).
- Collects modified directories in `self.modified_paths` for Jellyfin refresh.

Args:
  self: Instance of the execution view class.

Returns:
  None

Raises:
  Exception: Caught internally; emits `self.error.emit(str(e))` and logs error.
  FileNotFoundError: For missing source files (logged as failure).
  Any: Database or file operation errors are handled per-operation without halting batch.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: __init__
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Initialize the Execution View widget.

Sets up the real-time execution monitor for file operations with
transaction management, progress tracking, and rollback capabilities.
This view implements Points 6-9 of the JellyRancher workflow.

Args:
    project: The current Project instance
    project_manager: ProjectManager instance for database operations
    action_plan_id: Optional action plan ID to load immediately
    parent: Parent QWidget (typically the main application window)
    
The view provides:
- Real-time execution progress with visual progress bar
- Live transaction log with timestamps
- Execution controls (start, pause, stop)
- Rollback capability for failed operations
- Post-execution summary and statistics

If action_plan_id is provided, the view automatically loads
and prepares the action plan for execution.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _init_ui
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Initialize the user interface components for the execution monitor.

Creates and configures all UI elements:
- Progress section: `QProgressBar` (`self.progress_bar`) and status label (`self.lbl_status`).
- Snapshot section: Button (`self.btn_snapshot`) connected to `_create_snapshot`,
  read-only `QTextEdit` (`self.snapshot_info`).
- Mode checkboxes: Dry run (`self.chk_dry_run`, default checked, bold orange style),
  Jellyfin refresh (`self.chk_jellyfin_refresh`, default checked, blue style, initially disabled).
- Control buttons: Execute (`self.btn_execute`, green style, connected to `_start_execution`),
  Rollback (`self.btn_rollback`, red style, initially disabled, connected to `_rollback`).
- Log viewer: Read-only `QTextEdit` (`self.log_text`, monospace font).
- Summary label (`self.lbl_summary`).

The UI uses `QVBoxLayout` with sections in `QGroupBox` for organization:
header, progress, snapshot, modes, buttons, log, summary.
All margins, spacing, fonts, and stylesheets are applied for polished appearance.

Side effects:
- Sets `self` layout to the main `QVBoxLayout`.
- Connects button click signals to handler methods.

Args:
  self: Instance of the execution view class (QWidget subclass).

Returns:
  None

Raises:
  None

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _load_action_plan
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Load action plan details from the database.

Retrieves metadata about the current action plan including operation
counts, approval status, and execution state. This information is
used to configure the UI and determine available actions.

The method:
1. Validates that an action_plan_id is set
2. Queries the database for action plan metadata
3. Updates UI status labels with operation counts
4. Enables/disables buttons based on execution state
5. Shows appropriate messaging for executed plans

This ensures the UI reflects the current state of the action plan
and provides appropriate controls for the user's next actions.

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: If database operations fail

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _start_execution
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Start execution of approved operations.

Initiates the file operation execution process with appropriate
safety confirmations and mode selection (dry run vs production).

The method:
1. Validates that an action plan is selected
2. Checks dry run mode setting
3. Shows appropriate confirmation dialog based on mode
4. Creates and starts the ExecutionWorker thread
5. Disables execution controls during processing
6. Enables rollback capability

Dry run mode simulates all operations without actual file changes,
useful for testing the execution plan. Production mode performs
actual file operations with full transaction logging.

The confirmation dialogs include clear warnings about the
destructive nature of production execution.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warnings if no action plan is selected

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _on_progress
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Handle progress updates from the execution worker.

Updates the progress bar and status label with current execution
progress information. This method is called from the worker thread
to provide real-time feedback to the user about operation progress.

Args:
    current (int): Current operation number being processed (0-based)
    total (int): Total number of operations to process
    status (str): Descriptive message about current operation
    
The progress bar shows completion percentage, and the status label
displays the current operation being performed. This provides
visual feedback during potentially long-running operations.

Error Handling:
    If progress update fails, logs the error and attempts to set
    a fallback status message. If even that fails, logs the UI error.
    This prevents progress update failures from crashing the UI.

Thread Safety:
    This method is called from the worker thread and updates UI
    elements, which is safe in PyQt6 as long as signal-slot connections
    are used (which they are via the progress signal).

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _on_log_message
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Handle log messages from the execution worker.

Appends log messages to the execution log text area. This method
is called from the worker thread to provide detailed execution
feedback including operation details, transaction IDs, and status
updates.

Args:
    message (str): Log message to append to the execution log
    
The log messages include:
- Operation start/end notifications
- Transaction IDs for audit trail
- File operation results (success/failure)
- MD5 verification results
- Error details and recovery actions

Error Handling:
    If appending the message fails, logs the error to prevent
    log display failures from interrupting execution. This ensures
    execution continues even if UI logging encounters issues.

Thread Safety:
    Called from worker thread via signal-slot mechanism, safe
    for UI updates in PyQt6.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _on_finished
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Handle execution completion and update UI state.

Called when the execution worker completes all operations. Updates
the UI to reflect completion status, enables rollback capability,
and optionally triggers Jellyfin library refresh.

Args:
    success_count (int): Number of operations that completed successfully
    fail_count (int): Number of operations that failed
    batch_id (str): Unique identifier for this execution batch
    
The method:
1. Disables execution controls (execution cannot be restarted)
2. Re-enables dry run and Jellyfin refresh checkboxes
3. Stores the batch ID for rollback reference
4. Enables rollback button if production mode was used
5. Updates status label with completion summary
6. Triggers Jellyfin refresh if requested and available

Rollback is only enabled for production executions (not dry runs)
since dry runs don't modify actual files.

Jellyfin refresh updates the media library to reflect file changes,
ensuring the library stays synchronized with the filesystem.

Error Handling:
    All operations are wrapped in try-catch to prevent UI update
    failures from affecting the completion handling.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _on_error
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Handle execution errors and provide user feedback.

Called when the execution worker encounters a critical error that
prevents further processing. Updates UI state to allow retry and
shows error dialog to inform the user.

Args:
    error_msg (str): Description of the error that occurred
    
The method:
1. Re-enables execution controls so user can retry
2. Updates status label with error information
3. Shows critical error dialog with full error details
4. Logs any UI update failures to prevent secondary errors

Error handling ensures that even if UI updates fail, the error
is still logged and the user is informed through the dialog.
This prevents silent failures where users don't know execution
stopped due to an error.

The error dialog uses QMessageBox.critical to clearly indicate
a serious problem that requires user attention.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _rollback
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Rollback executed operations using TransactionManager.

Reverses all file operations from the most recent production execution batch
(`self.current_batch_id`), restoring files to original locations.
Provides safety net for failed or incorrect executions.

Process:
1. Checks if `self.current_batch_id` exists (shows warning if not).
2. Prompts confirmation dialog with batch ID and destructive warning.
3. Calls `TransactionManager.rollback_batch(self.current_batch_id, dry_run=False)`.
4. Appends detailed results (total, success, failed, errors) to `self.log_text`.
5. Disables `self.btn_rollback`.
6. Updates `self.lbl_summary` and shows info/warning dialog based on results.

Only available after production runs (dry runs skipped).
Uses transaction log for precise reversals.

Side effects:
- Moves files back via TransactionManager.
- Updates UI state and log.
- Logs to `logger`.

Args:
  self: Instance of the execution view class.

Returns:
  None

Raises:
  Exception: Caught; appends to log, shows critical dialog, and logs to `logger`.

scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.name: _create_snapshot
scripts\\ui\\execution_view.py.description:
Simulate creation of a transaction snapshot (legacy Step 6 from original workflow).

Displays educational text in `self.snapshot_info` about `TransactionManager` capabilities
and shows confirmation dialog. Provides user reassurance on safety features.

Snapshot info covers:
- Transaction/Batch IDs
- Source/Destination paths
- MD5 hashes before/after
- Operation types (move/copy/delete)
- Status tracking

Originally Step 6 in JellyRancher; now automated but retained for UI/education.

Side effects:
- Sets `self.snapshot_info.setPlainText(text)`.
- Shows info dialog.

Args:
  self: Instance of the execution view class.

Returns:
  None

Raises:
  Exception: Caught; logs to `logger` and shows critical dialog.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: __init__
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Initialize the Review View widget.

Sets up the interactive review interface for proposed file operations.
This view implements Point 5 of the JellyRancher workflow, providing
an Excel-like table for reviewing, approving, and editing action plans.

Args:
    project: The current Project instance containing analysis data
    project_manager: ProjectManager instance for database operations
    parent: Parent QWidget (typically the main application window)
    
Raises:
    Exception: If initialization fails, shows critical error dialog to user
    
Signals:
    operations_ready(int): Emitted when action plan is ready for execution
                         (passes action_plan_id)

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _init_ui
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Initialize the user interface components of the ReviewView.

Creates and configures a comprehensive review interface using PyQt6 widgets,
organized in a vertical QVBoxLayout with the following sections:

- Header: Title label 'Action Plan Review' with custom styling.
- Search and filter controls: QLineEdit for search and QComboBox for filters
  (All Operations, Approved Only, High Confidence (>=90%), Manual Review (70-89%),
  Moves Only, Renames Only). Search connects to _filter_operations, filter to
  _apply_filter.
- Button row: Load Action Plan (step_5_review), Export to CSV (_export_to_csv,
  initially disabled), Dry Run Preview (_dry_run_preview, disabled),
  Select All (_select_all), Approve Selected (_approve_selected, green styling),
  Reject Selected (_reject_selected, red styling), Preview Changes (_preview_changes).
- GroupBox 'Proposed Operations': QTableWidget with 10 sortable columns
  (Selection checkbox, Type, Current Path, Proposed Path, Confidence, Jellyfin Status,
  Current MD5, Proposed MD5, Notes, Approve checkbox), custom widths, interactive
  resizing. Summary QLabel below table.
- Execute button: '▶ Execute Approved Operations' (red styling, _execute_operations).

All layouts have margins and spacing. Table enables sorting.

Args:
    self: ReviewView instance.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Logs error, shows critical QMessageBox, and re-raises if widget
        creation, layout setup, or signal connections fail.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _load_analysis_data
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Load the most recent analysis metadata for the current project.

Retrieves the latest LLM analysis results from the database to provide
context for action plan generation. This includes detected media items
and analysis confidence scores.

The method:
1. Connects to the media library database
2. Queries for the most recent analysis for this project
3. Parses the stored JSON data (detected media, recommendations)
4. Loads any associated canonical metadata if available
5. Updates UI status to reflect loaded data

If no analysis data is found, the UI will show appropriate messaging
to guide the user to run analysis first.

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: If database operations fail
    json.JSONDecodeError: If stored analysis JSON is malformed

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _load_scanned_files
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Load scanned files from the most recent scan session.

Retrieves the file inventory from the latest scan session to provide
the complete list of files that can be operated on. This data is
essential for generating and validating action plans.

The method:
1. Queries the database for the most recent scan session
2. Extracts scan options including inventory session IDs
3. Loads all file records from associated inventory sessions
4. Updates the scanned_files list for use in action plan generation

This ensures that action plans are generated against the most current
and complete file inventory available.

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: If database operations fail
    json.JSONDecodeError: If scan options JSON is malformed

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: step_5_review
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Generate an action plan using the ActionPlanWorker.

This is the main entry point for Point 5 of the workflow: Action Plan Generation.
Creates a comprehensive set of proposed file operations based on LLM analysis,
canonical metadata, and scanned file inventory.

The method validates prerequisites:
1. Scanned files must be available
2. LLM analysis results must exist
3. Canonical metadata database must be built

Then initiates the action plan generation:
1. Creates and configures an ActionPlanWorker thread
2. Passes all required data (files, analysis, metadata)
3. Disables UI controls during processing
4. Shows progress indication

The worker runs asynchronously to prevent UI blocking. Results are
processed by connected signal handlers when complete.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warnings if prerequisites are not met

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _on_action_plan_finished
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Handle completion of action plan generation.

Processes the generated action plan and updates the UI to display
the proposed operations in the review table. This method is called
when the ActionPlanWorker completes successfully.

Args:
    action_plan: List of ProposedOperation objects representing
                the generated file operations to be reviewed
                
The method:
1. Stores the action plan in instance variables
2. Populates the review table with all proposed operations
3. Updates summary statistics and status messages
4. Enables export and preview functionality
5. Shows success notification to the user

The review table allows users to approve, reject, or modify
individual operations before execution.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows critical error if table population fails

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _on_action_plan_error
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Handle errors that occur during action plan generation.

This method is called when the ActionPlanWorker encounters an error
during operation generation. It provides user feedback and restores
the UI to a usable state.

Args:
    error_msg: Descriptive error message from the action plan worker
              (may include validation errors, processing failures, etc.)
              
The method:
1. Updates status label with error information
2. Shows a critical error dialog to inform the user
3. Logs the error for debugging purposes

Error handling is robust - if the error handler itself fails,
it includes fallback UI restoration to prevent the interface
from becoming unusable.

Common error causes:
- Invalid or inconsistent analysis data
- Metadata lookup failures
- File system access issues
- Configuration problems

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _populate_table
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Populate the operations table with data from self.operations list.

Clears and sets row count to len(self.operations). For each ProposedOperation:

- Column 0: QCheckBox (selection checkbox, no signal connection).
- Column 1: Operation type (str(op.action_type)).
- Column 2: str(op.source_path).
- Column 3: str(op.destination_path) or 'N/A'.
- Column 4: Confidence (str(op.confidence)) with background color:
  HIGH (green), MEDIUM (orange), else (red).
- Column 5: op.jellyfin_status or 'Unknown'.
- Column 6: op.current_md5 or 'N/A'.
- Column 7: op.proposed_md5 or 'N/A'.
- Column 8: op.notes or ''.
- Column 9: QCheckBox approve (initially True if HIGH confidence or op.user_approved,
  connects stateChanged to _on_approve_changed(row, state)).

Updates summary label with total, approved, pending counts. Handles per-row errors.

Args:
    self: ReviewView instance.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Logs error, shows critical QMessageBox, clears table if overall failure.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _on_approve_changed
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Handle changes to operation approval checkboxes.

Updates the user approval status for a specific operation when the
corresponding checkbox is checked or unchecked. This allows users
to selectively approve or reject individual operations.

Args:
    row: Table row index corresponding to the operation
    state: Checkbox state (Qt.CheckState.Checked.value or unchecked)
    
The method:
1. Validates the row index is within bounds
2. Updates the user_approved field on the ProposedOperation
3. Triggers summary statistics update
4. Shows error dialog if update fails

This provides the core interactivity for the review table,
allowing users to build custom action plans by approving
only desired operations.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warning if approval update fails

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _update_summary
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Update the summary label with current approval statistics.

Counts approved operations (op.user_approved is True) and displays:
'Total: {len(self.operations)} operations | Approved: {approved_count} |
Pending: {pending_count}'.

Provides real-time feedback during review.

Args:
    self: ReviewView instance.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Logs error and attempts fallback text 'Operations loaded
        ({len(self.operations)} total)', logs UI update failure if label inaccessible.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _select_all
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Select all rows by checking the selection checkboxes in column 0.

Iterates all table rows and sets cellWidget(row, 0) QCheckBox to checked.
Prepares rows for bulk approve/reject operations. Does not modify approve
checkboxes (column 9) or user_approved fields directly; use _approve_selected
or _reject_selected afterward.

Args:
    self: ReviewView instance.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Logs error and shows warning QMessageBox if table access or
        widget manipulation fails.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _approve_selected
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Approve selected rows by checking their approve checkboxes (column 9).

Iterates all table rows: if selection checkbox (column 0) is checked, sets
approve checkbox (column 9) to checked. Triggers _on_approve_changed via signal,
updating op.user_approved.

Args:
    self: ReviewView instance.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Logs error and shows warning QMessageBox if table or widget access fails.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _reject_selected
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Reject selected rows by unchecking their approve checkboxes (column 9).

Iterates all table rows: if selection checkbox (column 0) is checked, sets
approve checkbox (column 9) to unchecked. Triggers _on_approve_changed via signal,
updating op.user_approved to False.

Args:
    self: ReviewView instance.

Returns:
    None

Raises:
    Exception: Logs error and shows warning QMessageBox if table or widget access fails.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _filter_operations
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Filter operations table based on search text.

Dynamically hides/shows table rows based on whether they match
the search criteria. This allows users to quickly find specific
operations in large action plans.

Args:
    search_text: Text to search for in operation paths
                (case-insensitive substring matching)
                
The method:
1. Iterates through all table rows
2. If no search text, shows all rows
3. If search text provided, checks source and destination paths
4. Shows rows where search text is found in path columns
5. Hides rows that don't match the search criteria

Search is performed on:
- Source file path (column 2)
- Destination path (column 3)

This provides efficient navigation through large operation lists.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _apply_filter
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Apply advanced filtering based on selected filter criteria.

Provides sophisticated filtering options beyond simple text search,
allowing users to view operations by approval status or confidence level.

Args:
    filter_text: Filter criteria selected from dropdown
                Options: "Approved Only", "High Confidence (≥90%)",
                "Manual Review (70-89%)", "Low Confidence (<70%)"
                
Filter types:
- "Approved Only": Shows only user-approved operations
- "High Confidence (≥90%)": Shows operations with HIGH confidence
- "Manual Review (70-89%)": Shows operations needing manual review
- "Low Confidence (<70%)": Shows operations with LOW confidence

The method:
1. Iterates through all table rows
2. Applies the selected filter criteria
3. Shows/hides rows based on filter match
4. Updates visible row count

This helps users focus on specific types of operations
during the review process.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _preview_changes
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Preview the approved operations before execution.

Shows a detailed preview of all operations that have been approved
by the user. This allows final review of the changes before they
are actually executed on the file system.

The method:
1. Filters operations to include only approved ones
2. Validates that at least one operation is approved
3. Opens a preview dialog showing all approved operations
4. Displays source/destination paths and operation types

This provides a safety check to ensure users understand
exactly what changes will be made before execution.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warnings if no operations are approved

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _dry_run_preview
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Preview all operations for planning purposes.

Shows a complete preview of the entire action plan, regardless of
approval status. This is useful for understanding the full scope
of proposed changes during planning and review phases.

The method:
1. Validates that operations exist
2. Shows preview dialog with all operations
3. Displays complete action plan for review

Unlike _preview_changes, this shows all operations (approved and
unapproved) to give users a complete picture of what the action
plan contains, useful for strategic planning.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warnings if no operations exist

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _show_preview_dialog
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Display a preview dialog showing operation details.

Creates and shows a modal dialog with formatted details of the
provided operations. This gives users a clear, readable view
of what changes will be made.

Args:
    operations: List of ProposedOperation objects to display
    title: Dialog window title
    intro: Optional introductory text to display at the top
    
The dialog displays:
- Operation number and type
- Source and destination paths
- Confidence level
- Operation notes
- Formatted in a monospace font for readability

The dialog includes OK/Cancel buttons and is resizable for
viewing large numbers of operations.

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _export_to_csv
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Export the current action plan to a CSV file.

Saves all operations in the current action plan to a CSV file
for external review, backup, or processing. This allows users
to work with the action plan in spreadsheet applications.

The method:
1. Validates that operations exist to export
2. Opens a file save dialog with timestamped default filename
3. Writes CSV header row with column names
4. Exports all operation details as CSV rows
5. Shows success confirmation

CSV columns include:
- Operation type
- Source path
- Destination path
- Confidence level
- User approval status
- Notes

This provides a portable format for action plan review
and archival purposes.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows information if no operations to export

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _execute_operations
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Execute all approved operations.

This is the final step in the workflow: executing the approved
file operations on the actual file system. This permanently
modifies files according to the action plan.

The method:
1. Filters operations to include only approved ones
2. Validates that operations exist for execution
3. Shows confirmation dialog with operation count
4. If confirmed, saves action plan to database
5. Emits operations_ready signal to trigger execution
6. Shows success confirmation

This is a destructive operation that modifies the file system.
The confirmation dialog ensures users understand the consequences.

The operations are executed by the Execution View component
after receiving the operations_ready signal.

Raises:
    QMessageBox: Shows warnings if no operations are approved

scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.name: _save_action_plan_to_database
scripts\\ui\\review_view.py.description:
Save the complete action plan to the database.

Persists the reviewed and approved action plan for execution tracking
and audit purposes. This creates a permanent record of the operations
that will be executed.

The method:
1. Creates a new action plan record with summary statistics
2. Saves all individual operations with their approval status
3. Includes metadata like confidence levels and file hashes
4. Stores the action plan ID for execution tracking

Saved data includes:
- Action plan metadata (counts, timestamps)
- Individual operations with full details
- User approval decisions
- Confidence levels and notes
- File integrity information (MD5 hashes)

This provides a complete audit trail for the file operations
and enables execution by other components.

Raises:
    sqlite3.Error: If database operations fail
